notes.claim: Gas kept at constant temperature has pressure and volume varying so that PV is constant, which is Boyle's Law.
The work done by n moles of ideal gas expanding reversibly and isothermally is nRT ln(V2/V1).
The special case n = 1 of pV^n = constant is the isothermal expansion, where the work integral gives a natural logarithm.

The add-one-to-the-power, divide-by-the-power rule cannot integrate certain terms, because adding one to their power gives 0 (source's equation symbols did not come through: the terms are powers of -1).

sources.title: 8.3: Isothermal Expansion of an Ideal Gas - Physics LibreTexts
sources.quote: if a fixed mass of gas kept at constant temperature is compressed or allowed to expand, its pressure and volume will vary according to PV = constant. That is, Boyle's Law.
